title: What Makes a Shape a Shape?

steps.body: Every shape is a members-only club with **entry rules**. A triangle's rules: three straight sides, three corners, closed all the way around. Meet the rules, you're in — no matter your color or size. Those rules are the shape's **defining attributes**.

widget.prompt: Sort each feature of a triangle: is it an entry RULE (defining) or just a COSTUME (non-defining)?

items.label: Has exactly 3 sides
items.feedback: Change this and it stops being a triangle — a real entry rule.

items.label: Is painted red
items.feedback: Paint it blue and it's still a triangle — color is just a costume.

items.label: Has 3 corners
items.feedback: Three sides always bring three corners — a defining rule.

items.label: Is the size of your hand
items.feedback: Shrink it or grow it — still a triangle. Size is a costume, not a rule.

widget.missFeedback: Ask: if I change this, is it STILL a triangle? If yes, it's a costume; if no, it's a rule.
widget.successFeedback: Sides and corners are the entry rules; color and size are costumes the shape can swap freely.

explanationVariants: Color isn't an entry rule — a green triangle keeps all three sides and corners, so it's still a triangle.
Only the defining attributes (sides, corners, closed) decide membership; green is a costume.

widget.prompt: You paint a triangle green. Is it still a triangle?

options.label: Yes — color isn't one of the entry rules
options.feedback: Three sides, three corners, still closed — the rules are untouched. Color is just a costume.

options.label: No — triangles can't be green
options.feedback: The entry rules say nothing about color. A green, blue, or striped triangle still has three sides — still in the club.

options.label: Only if it's a small triangle
options.feedback: Size is also a costume, not a rule. Any color at any size, the three-sided rule is what counts.

options.label: It becomes a different shape
options.feedback: Painting changes only the look. To change the SHAPE you'd have to change sides or corners — the actual rules.

steps.body: Turning a shape doesn't break its rules either. A square balanced on one corner looks like a 'diamond,' but it still has **four equal sides and four square corners** — every rule intact. Rotation is a costume too; the club only checks sides and corners.

explanationVariants: Tilting changes only which way it faces — the four equal sides and four square corners are all still there, so it's still a square.
'Diamond' is just a tilted square; rotation is a costume, and the entry rules haven't changed.

widget.prompt: A square is turned to balance on one corner, so it looks like a diamond. What shape is it?

options.label: A square, just turned
options.feedback: Four equal sides, four square corners, just tilted. Rotation is a costume.

options.label: A diamond, a new shape
options.feedback: 'Diamond' is just the nickname for a tilted square — same four equal sides and square corners. The rules didn't change.

options.label: A triangle, just turned
options.feedback: Turning never adds or removes sides — it still has four, not three. A tilted square is a square.

options.label: A shape set by the corner
options.feedback: Any corner, same result: the sides and corners are unchanged by turning. Still a square.

widget.prompt: Tap every shape that follows the triangle rules (3 straight sides, closed) — ignore color and size.

hotspots.label: 4-sided shape
hotspots.feedback: This one has FOUR sides — that breaks the three-side rule. Not a triangle, whatever its color.

hotspots.label: open 3-line shape
hotspots.feedback: Three lines, but it isn't CLOSED — there's a gap. Closed-all-the-way is a triangle rule too.

widget.missFeedback: Check the RULES only: exactly 3 straight sides and closed. Color, size, and tilt don't matter.
widget.successFeedback: The three 3-sided closed shapes are triangles — even tilted or tiny. The 4-sided and the open one are out.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents attributes.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for attributes must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines attributes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: A defining attribute is one you can't change without changing the shape — the number of sides is the classic example.
Rules stay fixed for every member; costumes (color, size, tilt) vary freely.

widget.prompt: Which of these is a DEFINING attribute — an actual entry rule for a shape?

options.label: The number of sides
options.feedback: Change the side count and you change the shape itself — that's a rule, not a costume.

options.label: The color it's drawn in
options.feedback: Color changes nothing about membership — a costume. The number of sides is the real rule.

options.label: How big it is
options.feedback: Size is a costume — a shape stays itself at any size. The defining rule here is the side count.

options.label: Which way it's turned
options.feedback: Rotation is a costume too. Only features like side count define which club a shape belongs to.

hints: Ignore the color and size completely — those are costumes.
Count the straight sides and check it's closed.
Four straight sides, closed — which club is that?
explanationVariants: Strip away the costumes (huge, orange): it has four straight sides and is closed, so it's a quadrilateral — a four-sided shape. The color and size never mattered.
The only clues that count are the defining ones: 4 sides + closed = a four-sided shape (quadrilateral).

widget.prompt: A detective finds a HUGE ORANGE shape with 4 straight sides, closed all around. What kind of shape is it?

options.label: A quadrilateral with four sides
options.feedback: Four straight sides, closed — that's the rule that matters. Huge and orange are just costumes.

options.label: A triangle with three sides
options.feedback: Orange is a costume, not a shape type. The defining clue is 4 straight sides: a quadrilateral.

options.label: A circle with no straight sides
options.feedback: Size tells you nothing about sides — and this one has FOUR, not three. Four sides makes a quadrilateral.

options.label: A mystery with unknown sides
options.feedback: Color is exactly what to ignore. The 4 straight sides already name it: a four-sided shape.

takeaways: Defining attributes (sides, corners, closed) are a shape's entry rules.
Color, size, and tilt are costumes — they never change the shape.
To name a shape, check only its rules.
steps.teaser: next: the big four-sided family and the rules that split it up.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **A costume can change; a rule cannot.** Ask one question about any feature: 'If I change this, is it still the same shape?' Yes → costume (color, size, tilt). No → rule (number of sides and corners).

explanationVariants: A bigger square is still a square — size is a costume.
Changing size doesn't touch the four equal sides or square corners, so it stays a square.

widget.prompt: You make a square twice as big. Is it still a square?

options.label: Yes — size is a costume, not a rule
options.feedback: Same four equal sides and square corners, just bigger. Still a square.

options.label: No — big squares are a different shape
options.feedback: Size never changes the entry rules. A big square keeps all of them — still a square.

options.label: Only if you also turn it
options.feedback: Turning is a costume too. Neither size nor tilt changes the sides or corners — still a square.
